attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2023-01-15
Provider: Dr. James O'Brien, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Collapse after being stung by multiple insects while gardening in his backyard during a warm summer afternoon.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This patient with systemic mastocytosis and prior 2020 dental procedure hypotension and bronchospasm presents after gardening in his backyard during a warm summer afternoon. According to his neighbor, he was stung by multiple insects moments before suddenly clutching his chest and falling to the ground.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Tyrosine hydroxylase (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Systemic mastocytosis
- Allergic asthma
- Persistent allergic rhinitis
- Generalized anxiety disorder

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tonsillectomy (age 8)
- Wisdom teeth extraction (age 22)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg IM as needed for anaphylaxis (carry two at all times)
- Cetirizine 10 mg PO daily
- Famotidine 20 mg PO twice daily
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 50 mcg (2 sprays per nostril) daily
- Cromolyn sodium oral solution 200 mg PO four times daily (30 minutes before meals and at bedtime)

ALLERGIES:
Hymenoptera venom (bees/wasps) - anaphylaxis, Latex (natural rubber) - anaphylaxis, Dust mites, Timothy grass pollen

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: severe Hymenoptera venom allergy, hypertension
- Mother: asthma, allergic rhinitis
- Sister: atopic dermatitis, food allergies
- Paternal uncle: systemic mastocytosis

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: High school mathematics teacher.

VITAL SIGNS:
With a blood pressure of 75/45 mm Hg and a heart rate of 120/min

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On arrival to the emergency department, he is found to be obtunded
Physical examination reveals flushed skin, periorbital swelling, and diffuse bilateral wheezing. There is no trauma or seizure activity. His extremities are cool, and capillary refill is delayed.

PLAN:
Oxygen is administered via nonrebreather mask, and he is placed supine with intravenous access established. He does not respond to fluid bolus alone.

attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Priya Patel, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Sudden hypotension and bronchospasm occurring during a scheduled dental procedure.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
He is brought to the emergency department after developing sudden hypotension and bronchospasm during a dental procedure. He is treated with a sympathomimetic medication that quickly improves blood pressure and relieves airway obstruction.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Systemic mastocytosis
- Allergic asthma
- Persistent allergic rhinitis
- Generalized anxiety disorder

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tonsillectomy (age 8)
- Wisdom teeth extraction (age 22)

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Epinephrine auto-injector 0.3 mg IM as needed for anaphylaxis (carry two at all times)
- Cetirizine 10 mg PO daily
- Famotidine 20 mg PO twice daily
- Albuterol HFA inhaler 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing
- Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 50 mcg (2 sprays per nostril) daily
- Cromolyn sodium oral solution 200 mg PO four times daily (30 minutes before meals and at bedtime)

ALLERGIES:
Hymenoptera venom (bees/wasps) - anaphylaxis, Latex (natural rubber) - anaphylaxis, Dust mites, Timothy grass pollen

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Father: severe Hymenoptera venom allergy, hypertension
- Mother: asthma, allergic rhinitis
- Sister: atopic dermatitis, food allergies
- Paternal uncle: systemic mastocytosis

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Occasional (1-2 drinks per month). Occupation: High school mathematics teacher.

OTHER STUDIES:
In the days following, a research group studies how this drug resembles certain endogenous compounds produced in adrenal chromaffin cells and sympathetic nerve terminals. These compounds are synthesized from an amino acid precursor in a multistep pathway involving several enzymes in the cytoplasm and storage vesicles. The earliest committed step in this pathway determines the overall rate of production and requires a specific enzyme that is tightly regulated, as it sets the pace for downstream conversion into mediators responsible for cardiovascular and metabolic responses.
